editorial.headline: Designing the Health and Beauty Products People Depend On
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers specialist product design across medical, laboratory, cosmetic and beauty-equipment fields—open nationally to foreign investment, but unavailable for PMA registration in Bali today.
editorial.body:
This activity is the design and development of products used in health, cosmetics and laboratory settings. Its scope reaches from medical equipment, materials and hospital products to medical devices and prosthetics; from pharmaceutical and cosmetic products to cosmetic packaging and containers. It also includes the design of beauty-salon and toilet accessories, wigs and similar products. The work is not confined to sketches or physical prototypes: specialised software is expressly part of how these design activities are carried out.

The registration is available to businesses operating at micro, small, medium and large scale. That breadth matters because the code describes a professional design activity rather than a single finished product. A studio developing a prosthetic concept, a team shaping laboratory equipment, or a practice creating cosmetic containers can all sit within the same activity, provided the work is genuinely product design and development within the stated health, cosmetic or laboratory scope.

Across Indonesia, the activity permits foreign investment up to a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In other words, the national position allows full foreign ownership for this activity. That clarity should not be mistaken for a universal location result, however. Bali’s position is different: a foreign-owned company cannot register this activity there today. The Bali classification records it as blocked for PMA registration under the province’s risk-class rule.

The reason is specific. At large scale, OSS assigns every scope within this activity a Low or Medium-Low risk classification. Bali’s permanent, island-wide moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities from PMA registration. The block is tied to that Bali rule, announced in May 2026, rather than to a reduction in the national foreign-ownership ceiling. For founders, the practical reading is straightforward: the activity remains nationally open to full foreign ownership, yet Bali is presently closed to PMA registration for it.
